_meta.name: scrums-ds
_meta.description: Sorted UI, the Scrums.com console/field-ops design system. This file holds structure and rules; colours/typography/spacing values come from design-tokens.json v1.1. Theme variants (light/dark/blue) share these same token names — only values swap.
_meta.sourceOfTruth: code repository (React components + JSON tokens) — Figma is experimental iteration only

colors._note: Full palette lives in design-tokens.json. Structure only: one accent, one status colour, a 7-step ink ramp, a 4-step hair ramp, per-theme surfaces, plus three CONSTANT surfaces that never re-theme (notif/nav/footer).

accent._rule: blue is the ONLY accent — buttons, active nav, links, key figures

status._rule: green appears ONLY on the live-status dot

instrumentation._rule: terminal/telemetry surfaces (command and terminal templates, hero HUD chrome) alias the primary-blue scale (950/900/700/400/200) plus the shared status/warning/error scales — never a hardcoded hex — so terminal surfaces can't drift off the brand shade

colors._constantRule: constant surfaces are defined once in :root and never repeated inside a theme override — that's what keeps nav/notif/footer fixed across light/dark/blue

typography._note: Role-based families, each a numbered/named scale: heading-*, label-*, data-*, ui-*, body-*. data-* is the family for tabular telemetry.

heading-*.purpose: titles, section headers — Plex Mono 600, tightens letter-spacing as size increases

label-*.purpose: uppercase tracked UI labels, coordinates, addresses

body-*.purpose: long-form prose — the ONLY place Plex Sans is used

typography.monoVsSans: The base face is MONO (~95% of all text), with body-* as the one Plex Sans exception for prose. Most systems are sans-first with mono for code; this one is mono-first, so an agent must not default to sans.

body-default.note: a11y floor — never below 15px for prose

spacing._gaps: Indices skip deliberately (6,10,14,18-19,22...) — reserved so a value can be inserted later without renumbering.
spacing._rule: gridline gaps (the 1px shared border between compartments) are structure, not spacing — never drawn from this scale

rounded._note: A deliberate 2-value enum — radius caps at 3px everywhere, so there is no size-based radius ladder (no sm/md/lg/full).
rounded._rule: 3px is the MAX radius anywhere. Never exceed it. No pills (rounded-full does not exist in this system — badges/tags are square, not pill-shaped).

materials._note: A Material fuses radius and elevation into one property — 3 tiers only, because radius never varies (always {rounded.default}) and elevation is shadow-free. The structural RULES below still apply even though the value ladder is shorter.

material-surface.usage: resting compartments — cards, table cells, form fields

material-elevated.usage: menus, modals, dropdowns — ONE tier covers all of these; there are no separate menu/modal/fullscreen tiers

material-overlay.usage: backdrop behind an elevated surface (modal, drawer)

structuralRules: One property, not two — a component declares material="elevated", never sets border-width and accent-edge separately.
No stacking — two Materials never nest; a child needing more lift becomes its own Material, not a layered one.
Decorative, not semantic — role="dialog"/role="tooltip" is still set independently; Material carries zero ARIA meaning.
Lowest-tier-that-works wins — reach for material-surface before material-elevated.

grid._note: Grid is not an opt-in component: the gridline construction IS the default compartment method. The grid is built with gridlines, not gaps.
grid.technique: gap-as-gridline — 1px gap over a {hair-2}-coloured parent, cells filled {paper}. Adjacent compartments share a single hairline; zero visual gaps, no floating cards, no radius on the shared edge.
structuralRules: Columns/rows are set explicitly at all three breakpoints — no implicit fallback.
Reserve visible-gridline construction for compartments meant to read as an instrument panel; plain n-column content (card lists) can use an invisible CSS grid instead.
Never nest more than one level deep — overlapping guides become noise.

motion._note: Governed as decision logic — not a flat list of durations to pick from.
motion.defaultPosture: prefer 0ms (no motion) unless it clarifies a state change
motion.curve: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1) — the one shared ease for everything
motion.a11y: honour prefers-reduced-motion — all decorative motion (radar sweep, boot sequence) must have a static fallback

assets._note: The literal files an agent should fetch/import, never regenerate — kept as a separate top-level peer to foundations.

brandAssets.usage: use the official logo files only — never redraw, recolour or re-letter the mark; brand guidelines outrank this file on conflict

mono.source: Google Fonts (static weights — no variable-font axis published for this family)
mono._note: expanded from [400,500,600] — light(300)/bold(700) added so weight, not size, can carry legibility and hierarchy on high-impact brand layouts. A wght@300..700 variable-range request was tried first and silently dropped Mono from the Google Fonts response entirely (no variable axis exists for this family) — reverted to the explicit static weight list.

icons.style: Line — 24x24 viewBox, single-weight outline, no fills, stroke-width 2, round linecap/linejoin
icons._rule: Hard rule: every icon anywhere in the system is Untitled UI. No hand-drawn, redrawn, or approximated icons — import the real asset/component from @untitledui/icons rather than recreating its path data.

components._note: Every variant is a flat object of REFERENCES, not raw styling — the mechanism that makes this a system rather than a style guide.

emphasis._rule: siblings sharing typography + radius + height; differ only in fill/border treatment. (2 emphasis tiers today — tertiary and error are a documented gap.)

size._rule: default is unsuffixed — the unlabeled variant is always the default

state._rule: states are a fixed recipe applied once per component family, not hand-picked per instance

universalStates.disabled: opacity: 0.45, cursor: not-allowed — fixed recipe, no per-component override
universalStates.focusVisible: 2px {blue} outline, offset 2px — never removed, never replaced with an outline-color-only change

componentInventory._note: The real, live inventory from @scrums/sorted-ui (69 components across 14 groups) — grouped exactly as the library's own gallery groups them, not re-bucketed into a generic UI-kit taxonomy.
structuralObservations: Naming favours the concrete: PlanCard / BillingToggle / UsageRow are three distinct components inside 'pricing', not one PlanCard with three modes — containers and content stay separate components.

Status is inline-only in real production: StatusDot exists, but Feedback and Toast have not shipped as real @scrums/sorted-ui components yet. Target designs for both already exist as gap-doc illustrations on the docs site (see gapCatalog) — the design work is done, only the real build is outstanding.

No real demo-chrome component exists (Browser/Phone/Window mockups) — but gap-doc illustrations for Browser and Phone already exist on the docs site (see gapCatalog), same status as Feedback/Toast above.

gapCatalog._note: Components documented on the docs site as illustrative target designs (data-kind="gap", dgd-*-styled) — NOT real, live @scrums/sorted-ui components. Distinct from componentInventory above, which is production-only. A component appearing here means the design/spec work exists but the real build doesn't yet; check here before claiming a component 'doesn't exist' anywhere in the system, and check componentInventory before claiming one 'isn't real production yet'.

voiceAndContent.narrativeArc: OBSERVE → UNDERSTAND → ORCHESTRATE → DEPLOY → IMPROVE (never Problem → Solution → Benefits → Features → Pricing)
voiceAndContent.copyRegisterFormula: {system} · {real metric} · {real metric} — e.g. "TALENT · 400 operators · 21d ramp", never a narrated sentence like "Orchestrate talent: vetted engineers embedded in weeks."
voiceAndContent.eyebrowFormula: [{SEC-NN}] {CATEGORY} // {SUBJECT} — an address, not a section label like "Why Scrums.com"

dosAndDonts: DO share gridlines between adjacent compartments — zero visual gaps, no floating cards.
DO pair every status signal with a dot AND text — never colour alone.
DON'T use green outside the live-status dot.
DO use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on every data-* value.
DON'T set body prose below 15px (the documented a11y floor).
DO honour prefers-reduced-motion on every decorative animation.
DON'T mix rounded and sharp corners in the same view.
DO reference tokens ({colors.accent.blue}) in component definitions — never hardcode a hex value inline.
DON'T stack two Materials on one element — delegate extra lift outward to a new element.

suggestedShape._note: The v1 skeleton of this file — colours stay a swappable leaf so light/dark/blue can be re-themed without touching structure.
